prompt:
Write a freelance proposal (cover letter) from Tobias Reyne for the job below.

About the freelancer: 7 years experience; skills: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack, HTML and CSS

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: Migrate site from GoDaddy/WordPress to another host
I need to move my domain, currently hosted on GoDaddy and connected to WordPress, to an EU-based host. I also need to move my email which currently uses GoDaddy's Office 365 product.
</job>

Past projects you may mention (the ONLY experience you may claim):
(none)

Style:
- Open by briefly introducing yourself.
- Do not mention any specific past project or client.
- Write 300 to 380 words.

Output only the proposal text. Never add contact details or links.
text:
Hi, I’m Tobias Reyne, a full stack developer with 7 years of experience working with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS.

I can help you migrate your domain, WordPress-connected site, and GoDaddy Office 365 email to an EU-based host in a way that keeps the transition organized and low-risk. This kind of move needs careful handling so the website, DNS, and email services all continue working properly during and after the transfer. I’m comfortable coordinating the technical steps involved and making sure nothing important is overlooked.

For the website migration, I would review the current setup, identify what needs to be moved, and make sure the new hosting environment is ready before switching anything over. For the domain transfer, I’d handle the DNS details carefully so the domain points to the new host correctly. For email, I’d make sure the Office 365 migration is planned properly so you do not lose access to existing mailboxes or experience unnecessary downtime.

If needed, I can also help verify that any WordPress-related configuration is preserved during the move, including site access, DNS records, and mail routing. I pay close attention to the order of operations, since moving a domain and email together can create issues if things are changed too quickly. My goal is to keep the process smooth, clear, and secure.

I’d be glad to discuss your current setup, what EU-based host you want to move to, and whether you already have a preferred plan for email. From there, I can help map out the migration steps and carry them through cleanly.
